title: Capesize
summary: Iron ore rates on the West Australia to China route maintained an active presence, with Port Hedland and Dampier departures to Qingdao settling between USD 14.15/15.30 fio. In the Atlantic, Tubarao fixtures to Qingdao, including West Africa options, achieved between USD 37.25/37.50 fio.

title: Kamsarmax / Panamax
summary: In the Pacific, NoPac trips with Singapore-Japan options settled between USD 18,500/20,500 pd. Australian rounds with redelivery in South China and Singapore-Japan ranges fetched between USD 16,000/21,500 pd.

title: Ultramax / Supramax
summary: In the Pacific, a North China trip via NoPac to Australia settled at USD 19,000 pd, while a South China run to WCSA made USD 19,000 pd. Indonesian coal trips with options to India, China and regional destinations achieved between USD 15,000/23,000 pd, whereas steel, slag and clinker runs from North China to East Coast India range secured between USD 18,500/23,000 pd.

title: Handymax / Handysize
summary: In the Pacific, Indonesian clinker runs to South China and Taiwan settled at USD 15,000 pd, while a South East Asia trip via Australia to Singapore-Japan range also fetched USD 15,000 pd. A South China trip with Singapore-Japan options for 2 to 3 laden legs made USD 15,800 pd.

title: MARKET OVERVIEW
summary: Diplomatic discussions between regional authorities have introduced a new framework for managing the Strait of Hormuz, outlining a roadmap toward a temporary navigational channel and coordinated mine- clearing initiatives. Under this structure, negotiators are evaluating a dual-lane transit corridor where vessels would enter the Persian Gulf through northern designated waters and exit via southern lanes, followed by further discussions to establish permanent operational and security arrangements.

title: DRY BULK | BDI: 3,186 ▲12.14% (w-o-w)
summary: Dry bulk freight market demonstrated robust upward momentum, supported by tightening fleet availability and fresh weather disruptions across Asia even as critical maritime corridors face severe geopolitical strain. Ongoing conflicts have significantly constrained Black Sea agricultural shipments-with August wheat exports expected to fall well below 2.5 million tons compared to 6.3 million tons during the same period last year-while the blockage of the Strait of Hormuz has stalled crucial fertiliser trade and left an estimated 120 to 150 bulk carriers immobilised.

title: Segment Highlights
summary: **Capesize:** Capesize rebounded this week, driven by a surge in Western Australian iron ore shipments alongside prompt tonnage tightening as ballasters maneuvered around another incoming typhoon off southeast China. Active participation from major miners pushed Pacific C5 rates higher, while steady Guinean bauxite and iron ore stems helped absorb long-haul capacity to keep the Atlantic market well supported.
